pairs.difference: A: the cream telescope tube goes almost white against a flat mid-grey moon floor and pale stripes. In the lens almost the whole card falls into two light-mid levels, and the only darks are thin tripod legs (rms 0.094, below the real range). B: the binoculars' near-black eyepiece rings and barrels set hard dark accents against a light plank floor. The value groups are clear, like the real camera card.
pairs.fix: Darken the ground into a deeper grey-blue with a strong cast shadow under the tripod, make the tube a warmer mid cream rather than white, and add a dark eyepiece and dark tripod feet as the darkest accents.

pairs.difference: A: a bright white dome and tube sit on an even mid-grey ground. A uniform dark band of sky runs across the top, and the darks are only small crater shadows, so the hero separates as one white blob with a soft value grip. B: the tiki bar has big dark masses (hut interior, the shadowed stools in the pool) against light counters and roof, giving strong light/mid/dark groups.
pairs.fix: Shade the dome base and tube into mid greys on their shadow side, give the hero a dark cast shadow on the ground, and lighten the sky band toward the horizon so the top isn't one flat dark strip.

pairs.difference: A: a white rover body sits inside a near-white burst halo, so the hero melts into the glow behind it. The only darks are four black wheels at the bottom, and the overall key is at the top of the real range (0.73). B: the taxi is light against a mid-grey burst and dark road, with dark windows and tyres spread through the hero, which reads like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Tone down the bright glow behind the rover to a mid green, shade the rover's side panels a step darker than its top, and darken the ground under it with a firm shadow.

pairs.difference: A: a light grey console on light grey metal floor tiles makes a very high key (0.766, above the real range). Hero and floor share the same value group, and the top background is only a mid band. B: the popcorn cart has a dark red base and a dark blue background against white awning stripes, giving clear dark, mid and light groups.
pairs.fix: Make the floor a darker steel grey with a deep shadow under the console, put a darker background behind the top, and keep the console front a mid grey so it separates from the floor.

pairs.difference: A: a dark red scarf sits on light blue swirls. The hero is one clean dark group with soft shading and a light badge accent. B: the asteroid breaks into blotchy patches of three grey levels with no clear lit side and shadow side. The dark pooling under it is ragged, and the flames read as the same mid as the background waves.
pairs.fix: Light the rock from one side, with a clear bright top-left face, a mid core and a dark underside, and make the flames brighter than the background.

pairs.difference: B: the planet and ring go clipped white against dark purple stripes. The hero is far lighter than the background (gap 0.247, beyond the real range), there's no shading on the ring and no corner falloff. A: the flip-flops are a light group on light teal stripes with mid-grey soles and a soft shadow, a high key but with value roll-off on the straps.
pairs.fix: Shade the ring and planet with a mid-tone shadow side and a soft roll-off rather than flat white, and lift the purple stripes a step so the hero isn't a white cut-out on near-black.

pairs.difference: A: flowers are tightly packed in mid greys inside a light stone ring, with low overall contrast (0.108). B: a mid-dark chair seat and back sit against a bright spotlight pool on the floor and wall, with a glow behind the hero. Both patterns appear in the real set (low-contrast pink arch, spotlit drum kit), so my vector gives no clear reason to choose.

A: a white helmet sits on a white table against a light pink wall. The hero and setting share one light value group (gap 0.028), the visor is a mid grey, and there's almost no dark anywhere. B: the sneakers are mid-dark blue against a light wall and floor, with a clear dark cast shadow, so the hero separates by value.
pairs.fix: Make the table a mid grey with a dark shadow under the helmet, darken the background wall to a deeper magenta, and make the visor a deep amber so it is the darkest area on the card.

pairs.difference: A: a pale white dish and light grey tower stand on near-white sand under a light sky. The card is one bright light-mid wash (0.794, rms 0.092), with only a thin shadow under the base. B: the sandcastle is also high key, but it has dark window openings, a dark arch and a mid sea band behind it, so there are more value steps inside the hero.
pairs.fix: Shade the dish underside and the tower's shadow side into clear mid-dark greys, add a long dark shadow on the sand, and make the sky a deeper blue so the white dish separates.

pairs.difference: A: a grey saucer sits on very light yellow rings, with a near-white glow right behind the hero. The overall key is above the real range (0.813), and the darks are only the rim band. B: a white player and earbuds sit on darker purple rings with a softer lighter centre, giving a clear light hero against a mid-dark field.
pairs.fix: Darken the yellow rings toward the corners to a deep orange, remove the white halo behind the saucer, and give the dome a darker green core.

pairs.difference: A: the bright yellow submarine is near white in the lens against a near-black green background with heavy dark corners. The hero-background gap is 0.322, far beyond the real range, which makes the card a hard spotlit cut-out. B: the rocket is mid-light against a light burst on mid blue. That is a gentle separation, like the real glove card.
pairs.fix: Lift the green background to a mid green with only slight corner darkening, and add mid-tone shading on the submarine's lower hull so it isn't a flat bright shape on black.

pairs.difference: A: a light golf club and ball sit on mid-light grass with white clouds behind. The key is bright but the dark grip and grass shadows add accents. B: an umbrella is lit on its top segments and dark underneath, on flat mid-blue rings, with low overall contrast (0.086). Both have features seen in the real set, and my vector gives no firm reason to pick either.

pattern: The generated cards are usually high key, with the hero in the same light value group as its background: a white hero on light floors, sky or a glow halo. Darks are few, small and confined to wheels, rims or tripod legs. The opposite failure also shows up: a clipped white hero on near-black stripes or a dark vignette, giving a hero-background gap outside the real range. Real cards keep a mid background with clear dark accents inside and under the hero, and shade the hero with a gentle roll-off.
